title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in Blazor WebAssembly Debugging Target Picker UI
analysis:
The Blazor WebAssembly debugging middleware maps the `/_framework/debug` endpoint. When a request is made, `TargetPickerUi.Display` reads the `url` query parameter as `targetApplicationUrl`. If retrieving debuggable browser tabs fails (e.g., if the browser isn't currently running with remote debugging active), an exception is caught. In the `catch` block, the raw, unencoded `targetApplicationUrl` is passed to `GetLaunchChromeInstructions` and `GetLaunchEdgeInstructions` and then directly written into the HTTP response stream with `ContentType = "text/html"`. This allows an attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the user's browser by crafting a malicious link with HTML/JS payload in the `url` parameter.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload:
```http
GET /_framework/debug?url=%3C/code%3E%3Cscript%3Ealert(document.domain)%3C/script%3E HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:5000
```
When this request is processed and `GetOpenedBrowserTabs()` fails (which is the default behavior if the developer hasn't manually opened a debugging port on Chromium), the unencoded payload in the `url` query parameter is rendered inside the instruction templates and sent back to the client as HTML, executing the script.
snippet:
await context.Response.WriteAsync($@"

Unable to find debuggable browser tab

Could not get a list of browser tabs from {debuggerTabsListUrl}. Ensure your browser is running with debugging enabled.

Resolution

If you are using Google Chrome or Chromium for your development, follow these instructions:

{GetLaunchChromeInstructions(targetApplicationUrl.ToString())}

If you are using Microsoft Edge (80+) for your development, follow these instructions:

{GetLaunchEdgeInstructions(targetApplicationUrl.ToString())}

This should launch a new browser window with debugging enabled..

Underlying exception:

{ex}
");
